name: Coldpatch Elder Coat & Walk Set
description: A full-length greatcoat in what was once a deep charcoal wool blend, now faded to a complex mix of grays and near-browns from years of acid rain, hand-washing, and sun exposure in the Gray Zone's filtered, dirty light. The coat falls to mid-calf and was clearly once a higher-tier garment — the construction quality beneath the damage is visible in the structured shoulders, the deep lapels, and the deliberate drape. It has been repaired so extensively that the repairs have become its primary visual identity: the left shoulder sports a large patch in rubberized olive canvas, its edges sealed with silver-gray self-repair tape folded into a clean border; the right sleeve carries three sequential patch repairs in progressively darker fabrics — charcoal, then near-black, then a strip of industrial gray rubber — recording years of acid-sleeve damage. The lining is entirely replaced, now a salvaged thermal blanket material in reflective silver, visible at the hem and collar as a glinting inner layer. The coat is belted with a wide leather strap that has been broken and re-stitched twice, the repair points marked by darker color where the leather was wetted and recured. Beneath the coat, a heavyweight turtleneck in faded ash marled knit sits close to the body, its ribbing loose at the collar from stretching but intact everywhere else. Wide-leg trousers in washed near-black canvas carry side-seam pockets and a reinforced seat. Footwear is a tall boot, resoled so many times the sole is now nearly an inch thick with layered rubber, the upper a patchwork of original leather and replacement panels in synthetic suede, the whole thing treated with a heavy waterproofing compound that gives it a waxy, uneven finish. A wide-brim hat in felted gray, its crown creased and its brim slightly warped but functional, completes the silhouette. The hat carries a single ornament: a small, carefully-polished piece of chrome scrap — possibly from a salvaged aug-component — pinned to the band.
functionality: Full-length acid-rain protection from rubberized patches and thermal blanket lining; reflective interior lining for passive heat retention; resoled boots for maximum sole durability on rough terrain; wide-brim hat for acid-rain facial protection; chrome ornament is a functional pin repurposed as decoration; large coat pockets carry significant storage
what_it_says: Age. History. Survival across multiple the Gray Zone seasons. This coat is an archive — each patch is a date, an incident, a cost survived. The original quality of the coat beneath the repairs suggests the wearer either came down from a higher tier or inherited something that outlasted its original context. The polished chrome ornament is the detail that matters: in a rig built entirely from necessity, one thing has been kept clean and bright. That's a statement about what the wearer values, and it isn't survival — it's dignity.
worn_by: long-term residents who have survived multiple acid seasons
people who came down from Tier 2 or 3 and never went back
informal the Gray Zone historians and keepers of local memory
manufacturer: Base coat is an unidentified pre-existing garment, likely Tier 3 manufacture, date unknown; all modifications self-made; boots are multi-source resoled originals
price_range: Φ 30–60 for the full set; the coat alone may be worth Φ 40–80 to the right collector
story_hooks: The chrome ornament on the hat band is identifiable to anyone who knows aug-tech: it's a fragment of a specific neural port housing from a model discontinued fifteen years ago — the same model involved in a mass-recall scandal that killed people in the Gray Zone. The wearer knows exactly what it is.

Someone from Tier 3 recognizes the base coat — it was a specific garment from a specific time, and seeing it on a the Gray Zone elder raises questions about who this person was before, and what they know.

The coat's inner lining — the salvaged thermal blanket — is stamped with a Lazarus Emergency Response batch number from a disaster relief distribution that officially covered a different district entirely. The wearer received it from someone. That someone may still be alive.

physical_description.visual_profile: A weathered, dignified silhouette that reads as lived-in wisdom rather than poverty. The full-length greatcoat dominates, its architectural shoulders and deliberate drape suggesting former corpo or professional origins. The patchwork of repairs creates an almost textile archaeology across the fabric — each patch tells a story of survival in the acid-rain the Gray Zone. The overall impression is of someone who has endured and adapted rather than surrendered. The chrome pin catches light like a final small claim to dignity.
physical_description.fit: Structured and tailored through the shoulders, relaxing into a generous, protective drape at the torso and legs. The coat falls mid-calf with intentional length. The turtleneck fits close and supportive. Trousers are full-legged without excess — functional rather than fashionable. Boots are sturdy and grounded, weighted by their many soles.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-blend base coat (original), rubberized canvas and industrial fabrics (patches), thermal blanket lining (reflective silver), marled knit turtleneck, washed canvas trousers, layered rubber soles, treated leather and synthetic suede boots, felted wool hat
physical_description.texture: Highly varied and tactile. The coat surface is soft where original, stiffened where patched with canvas or rubber. Edges of patches are sealed smooth with self-repair tape. The lining gleams with reflective texture. The turtleneck is loose and comfortable. Boot leather is waxy and slightly sticky from waterproofing compound. Hat felt is dense and worn smooth at high-contact points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: deep faded grays and near-browns, the original charcoal degraded by environmental exposure. Accent patches in olive canvas, charcoal, near-black, industrial gray rubber. Silver-gray repair tape and silver reflective lining visible at edges. The leather belt darkened and aged. Boots in mottled neutrals with waxy finish. Hat in soft felted gray. Single chrome accent on hat band.
closures: Coat: appears to use original button closures (not visible in description but implied by greatcoat construction)
Wide leather belt: appears to use buckle or tie closure, with evidence of re-stitching
Boots: likely lace or side-zip closure (resoled originals)
No magnetic or high-tech closures — purely mechanical/traditional
distinctive_features: Extensive visible patch map across shoulders and right sleeve, each layer recording years of acid-rain damage
Reflective silver thermal-blanket lining visible at collar and hem — functional but accidentally elegant
Twice-repaired leather belt with visible wet-cure repair marks
Boots with visible layered sole reaching nearly one inch thick
Single polished chrome salvage component pinned to hat band — personal memento or aug-scrap repurposed as jewelry
Marled ash turtleneck with stretched collar — evidence of long wear but structural integrity maintained
Wide-brim hat with subtle warp, functionally maintained
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 transitional. The original coat quality signals Tier 2-3 manufacture, but the extent and pragmatism of repairs, the salvage-sourced lining, and the resoled boots mark this as currently worn by someone operating in sub-grade or street margins. The garment is maintained, not abandoned — dignity preserved through labor rather than Φ.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by a survivor of the Gray Zone — someone with institutional memory (the coat's original quality), practical skills (all repairs self-made), and emotional grounding (the chrome pin, the care taken with seal-tape borders). This is likely an elder or long-term undercity resident, possibly someone who remembers pre-the Gray Zone conditions. The outfit signals street authority, careful self-reliance, and refusal to be discarded. Not corpo, not corpo-aspirant. Outside the system.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered, worn, extensively patched, but meticulously maintained. Not trash, not nostalgic vintage — actively lived-in. The self-repair tape is clean and functional. The lining is preserved. The boots are heavy-duty functional despite their age. This is a garment that will continue to be worn and repaired for as long as possible.
